list.listitem: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is caused by various diseases which result in elevated pulmonary artery pressures. The World Health Organization (WHO) classifies pulmonary hypertension into 5 groups based on the etiology.C
Suspect PH in patients who present with exertional dyspnea and signs of right heart failure such as dependent edema, abdominal distention, early satiety, angina, near syncope, and syncope.C

2D echocardiogram is the initial test of choice for the evaluation of pulmonary hypertension. Peak tricuspid regurgitant jet velocity >3.4 m/s on 2D ECHO indicates a high probability of PH. Ventilation perfusion scan is the test of choice for the evaluation of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH).C

Group 1 pulmonary hypertension can be managed medically. High dose calcium channel blockers are recommended in patients with PAH who respond to acute vasoreactivity testing. For patients with WHO functional class II and III using monotherapy or combination therapy with ambrisentan, bosentan, sildenafil, riociguat and IV epoprostenol has the best evidence.C
Group 4 pulmonary hypertension is managed primarily by pulmonary thromboendarterectomy.C

background.definition: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) refers to a group of serious and often progressive diseases of the pulmonary vasculature which can lead to right ventricular failure and eventually death. According to the 6th World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension (WSPH), PH is defined as a mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) greater than 20 mmHg.

list.listitem: The annual incidence of PH is 28.7 cases per/100,000 based on the results of a Canadian study.

The incidence of Group 1 PH (pulmonary arterial hypertension or PAH) is between 2.3 - 14 patients per million per year based on a systematic review that included single and multicentered studies from the United States.
The estimated incidence of Group 1 PH (PAH) among various countries in Europe, Asia and United States is 5.8 patients/million per year.
Based on a meta-analysis, the incidence of CTEPH after pulmonary embolism is 3.13%.The incidence of CTEPH in the general population is 3.1 - 6.0 ppm.

Overall, the global prevalence of PH is estimated to be around 1% but it may be as high as 10% in individuals older than 65 years. The prevalence of PH differs among the various causes of PH and is likely underestimated because etiology is not always established in all cases.
Based on a Canadian study the annual prevalence of PH is 127 cases/100 000 population.

The most common form of PH is due to heart disease. Globally over 100 million people have this type, which is referred to as Group 2 PH. Group 3 PH is the second most common form of PH and is due to lung diseases. A much smaller percentage of PH is caused by the other groups, mostly Groups 1 and 4.

The prevalence of Group 1 PH (pulmonary arterial hypertension or PAH) among United States patients is between 13 - 93 patients per million (ppm). Prevalence differs among subsets of patients with certain conditions. For example, prevalence of PAH among patients with HIV is 3% to 14%. Among patients with systemic sclerosis it is 5% to 8%
Estimated prevalence of Group 1 PH (PAH) in the United Kingdom, Ireland, and France ranges from 6.6-15 ppm.
PH can be present in up to 86% of patients suffering from interstitial lung disease. Prevalence of PH among patients with advanced pulmonary fibrosis referred for lung transplant is 25%.
Among select populations of patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) such as those referred for lung reduction surgery, prevalence of PH is up to 50%.
Prevalence of group 4 PH across various countries ranges from 25.8 - 38.4 ppm..
The classification of pulmonary hypertension has evolved since the first world symposium on pulmonary hypertension in Geneva, Switzerland in 1973.
According to the 6th WSPH Pulmonary hypertension can be classified into five groups as summarized below. Based on the etiology, each group is further divided into subgroups, as summarized in .
Causes of group 1 PH can be divided into hereditable and non-hereditable causes. Several genes are implicated in the pathogenesis of PAH, the three most common genes are BMPR2, TBX4 and ATP13A3.

Drugs associated with PAH are divided into “definite”, and “possible” categories to help monitor patients on drugs which require specific surveillance. Drugs in the definite category include Aminorex, Fenfluramine, Dexfenfluramine, Methamphetamines and Dasatanib. Drugs included in the possible category are Cocaine, Amphetamines, Interferon, Alkylating agents, Bosutinib and St. John’s wort.

Systemic sclerosis and HIV are both associated with PAH. Congenital heart diseases with Eisenmenger's syndrome, persistent systemic – pulmonary shunts, those with small, coincidental defects and patients who underwent defect correction have a higher risk of PAH.

Exposure to the stated risk factors may result in disruption of three major signaling pathways i.e., nitric oxide pathway, thromboxane A-2 pathway and the endothelin pathway.
Nitric oxide (NO), synthesized in the endothelial cells is responsible for smooth muscle relaxation and pulmonary vasodilation. Decreased bioavailability of NO in PAH may result in increased pulmonary vascular pressures. Prostacyclin's are anti-inflammatory agents produced in the endothelial cells which have antiproliferative and anti-thrombotic effects. PAH is associated with increased thromboxane A 2 synthesis which is both proinflammatory and prothrombotic Endothelin 1, which is produced in the endothelium, is a vasoconstricting agent. In PAH there is altered expression of endothelin receptors on smooth muscle and endothelial cells. This results in vasoconstriction and decrease in NO synthesis, respectively.
The above pathways result in increased pulmonary arteriolar constriction, endothelial remodeling, smooth muscle and endothelial cell proliferation as well as thrombus formation.
The pathophysiology of PAH is summarized in figure. These pathways also serve as targets for therapy

listitem.strong: Group 2 PH - PH due to left heart disease

list.listitem: Increased left atrial pressures may result from myocardial (HFrEF or HFpEF), valvular, congenital, or acquired cardiovascular conditions. Increased transmission of the left atrial pressures to the pulmonary vasculature results in increased pulmonary vascular pressures.
Increase in the retrograde pressures result in remodeling of both pulmonary arterial and venous structures. Remodeling is driven by damage to the endothelial cells with subsequent inflammation.
Patients with left heart disease and elevated left heart pressures may lead to increases in pressure in the pulmonary circulation.
Capillary injury occurs due to elevated retrograde pressures and triggers an inflammatory response causing proliferation of fibroblasts and thickening of the alveolar membranes.

Endothelial cell function is altered due to the elevated retrograde pressures, resulting in increased endothelin 1 secretion (vasoconstriction) and decreased nitric oxide (vasodilation). In addition to the effects of vasoactive mediators, endothelial cell damage results in smooth muscle proliferation in the pulmonary vascular system. These various mechanisms contribute to the increase in the pulmonary arterial pressures.

listitem.strong: Group 3 PH - PH due to lung disease, hypoxia, or both

list.listitem: Causes include airway disease (obstructive/restrictive), parenchymal disease and hypoxia.

Patients with group 3 PH have a loss of pulmonary capillary beds secondary to underlying lung disease. Loss of pulmonary vasculature results in an overall increase in resistance. Thus, decreased capacity to accommodate the same amount of flow (cardiac output) results in high pulmonary vascular pressures.

In contrast to systemic vasculature, normal physiological response of the pulmonary vasculature to hypoxia is vasoconstriction. Chronic hypoxia may contribute to increased pulmonary vascular resistance secondary to vasoconstriction.

In addition to the above mechanisms, it has been proposed that underlying disease processes may cause vascular abnormalities which are driven by increased inflammatory mediators and vasoactive mediators like PAH.

listitem.strong: Group 4 PH – Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension

list.listitem: Conditions such as hypercoagulable states (factor V Leiden, protein c and protein s deficiency), history of cancer and having a non-O blood group, predispose to an increased risk for CTEPH.

Thrombus resolution in some patients with pulmonary embolism does not occur as completely as expected. Unresolved thrombi eventually become organized and fibrosed. PH occurs because of obstruction due to organizing thrombi in proximal vessel.

Small vessel disease in patients with CTEPH is explained by blood flow that is redirected into the smaller vessels exposing them to higher pressures. This high pressure and shear stress causes endothelial cell dysfunction and increased pulmonary vascular resistance.
The role of nitric oxide and cGMP pathway in CTEPH is still being investigated. This pathway is also a target for medical therapy in patients with CTEPH who are not surgical candidates.

listitem.strong: Group 5 PH - pulmonary hypertension due to unclear multifactorial mechanisms

list.listitem: As the name suggests, it results from unclear or multifactorial mechanisms.

Some causes of Group 5 pulmonary hypertension are hematologic disorders (myeloproliferative disorders, sickle cell disease and chronic hemolytic anemia), systemic disorders (sarcoidosis, Langerhans cell histiocytosis), metabolic (thyroid disease, glycogen storage disorders, and Gaucher's disease) and others (patients on dialysis).
Routine screening for pulmonary hypertension (PH) is not recommended for the general population. C
Screening for pulmonary hypertension can be done in certain groups such as those with family history of PH, history of scleroderma and other high-risk groups using 2D echocardiography.C
Experts also recommend screening for pulmonary hypertension in adults with congenital heart disease.C
Suspect PH in patients who present with exertional dyspnea and signs of right heart failure such as dependent edema, abdominal distention, early satiety, angina, near syncope, and syncope.C
2D echocardiogram is the initial test of choice when considering the diagnosis of pulmonary hypertension.C

All patients with PH (idiopathic, hereditary and drug related) should have right heart catheterization with acute vasoreactivity testing to confirm the diagnosis, determine severity, and to help guide the initial therapy.A
In patients suspected of having PH due to chronic thromboembolism a ventilation perfusion scan should be the initial test of choice.C
According to the 6th World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension (WSPH), PH is defined as a mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) greater than 20 mmHg.

Isolated increases in mPAP > 20 mmHg is not diagnostic of PH because mPAP can be elevated due to other reasons including high cardiac output states. Hence other data points such as pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) must be used to characterize and to help define the underlying pathological process.
Three hemodynamic profiles have been described by the WSPH, namely isolated precapillary, combined pre and post-capillary, and isolated post-capillary PH.

According to the 6th WSPH Pulmonary hypertension can be classified into five groups. Depending on clinical presentation, pathological findings, and hemodynamic profiles the five groups are - Group 1: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) Group 2: PH due to left-sided heart disease Group 3: PH due to lung diseases and/or chronic hypoxia Group 4: Chronic thromboembolic PH Group 5: Pulmonary hypertension due to unclear multifactorial mechanisms
Pulmonary hypertension (PH) may be asymptomatic early in the disease process or present with non-specific symptoms such as dyspnea, fatigue, chest pain and palpitations.
As the disease progresses patients may experience symptoms of right heart failure such as lower extremity swelling, presyncope and syncope.
In PAH dyspnea tends to be the most common presenting symptom.

A detailed history should include personal history of lung disease (COPD, interstitial lung disease), heart disease (heart failure, Iichemic events), rheumatologic disease (scleroderma, Raynaud's phenomenon), and vascular disease (venous thromboembolism).

Family history is important in the identification of patients with hereditary pulmonary artery hypertension. In a large cohort of patients with PAH, 5.5% reported a family history of PAH and 15.3% patients had confirmed causal mutations.
A thorough occupational history that includes exposure to harmful chemicals and dusts may provide valuable information regarding the possible etiology of PH in patients with underlying lung diseases.

Physical exam findings suggestive of PH include a loud P2 component of the second heart sound, prominent and wide splitting of the second heart sounds, jugular venous distension and hepatojugular reflux.

Underlying diseases like chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and interstitial lung disease will have their typical physical findings. Patients with associated connective tissue disease may have arthralgias, joint swelling, or Raynaud phenomenon.

Although routine blood testing may not be helpful in the diagnosis of PH, some tests may help determine the underlying etiology of the PH. For example, thyroid function testing (often abnormal in group 1 PAH), Iron studies, and ferritin may indicate underlying hemochromatosis.
Serologic testing is helpful in the diagnosis of underlying infectious (HIV) and autoimmune diseases for example scleroderma.
Patients diagnosed with CTEPH should be tested for hypercoagulable states and thrombophilia using anticardiolipin antibody, lupus anticoagulant and anti β2 glycoprotein antibodies.

Several genes have been identified as causal factors for PAH, the most commonly associated genes in hereditary PAH are BMPR2 (bone morphogenic protein receptor), TBX4 (T box 4), ATP13A3 (ATPase 13 A 3).

Although a normal ECG does not rule out PH, important findings such as right axis deviation, right atrial enlargement (RAE), right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH), and right ventricular strain pattern point towards a diagnosis of PH.
Surface electrocardiogram is not a reliable tool in screening for right ventricular hypertrophy due to its low sensitivity.
An Isolated decrease in diffusion capacity of carbon monoxide can be seen in patients with PH.
Pulmonary function testing may help identify obstructive or restrictive lung diseases that may contributing to PH.
A 2D echocardiogram is the first noninvasive test used to evaluate patients suspected of having PH.

The peak tricuspid regurgitant jet velocity, in addition to other echocardiographic signs of PH such as right ventricle (RV) size, interventricular septum flattening, RV outflow time, pulmonary regurgitation, PA diameter, right atrial area and inferior vena cava (IVC) diameter variation with respiration are used to classify the echocardiographic probability of PH.

Echocardiographic probability of PH is considered high if the peak tricuspid regurgitant jet flow is greater than 3.4m/sec alone or there is a flow between 2.9 - 3.4 and there are other 2D echocardiographic signs of PH.

In advanced COPD, echocardiography has a low sensitivity (43%) but high specificity (88%) for the diagnosis of PH (LR+ 3.9, LR- 0.64). Its performance improves when ruling out severe COPD-PH. This performance correlates inversely with lung hyperinflation.

Use of peak tricuspid jet flow alone may be inaccurate if probability is not high, hence the need for a comprehensive echocardiographic evaluation of other echocardiographic variables. Based on these echocardiographic variables the probability of PH based on 2D echocardiogram ranges from low, intermediate to high. See .
Chest X ray features of PH include dilated pulmonary arteries at the hilum and enlarged right atrium. Pruning may also be seen with decreased vascular markings in the lung periphery.
Chest radiography may also help rule other diagnosis with clues which point to the underlying lung or heart pathology such as COPD and heart failure.
A normal chest radiograph does not rule our pulmonary hypertension.
Findings that offered a sensitivity >80 % for chest X ray were, Hilar size >112mm, projection of right heart border more than 44 and hilum chest ratio more than 0.44.
A ventilation perfusion scan is the screening test of choice when CTEPH is suspected. Sensitivity of VQ scan in detection of CTEPH (96%) is higher than that of CTA (51%).

Different imaging modalities such as VQ SPECT (Single photon emission CT) and V/Q planar scintigraphy have similar sensitivities around 98%. However, specificity of CTA for CTEPH is higher (96%) compared to VQ scanning modalities.
A chest high resolution chest CT scan can help identify parenchymal lung diseases which may be the cause of PH and may help differentiate group 3 PH from the other groups.

CT findings suggestive of PH include
Vascular signs: wall-adherent intraluminal thrombi, intraluminal webs/bands, abrupt vessel cutoffs, stenoses and wall irregularities Pulmonary artery (PA): PA diameter ≥ 2.9 cm or main pulmonary artery/ascending aorta ratio ≥ 1. Mosaic perfusion: areas of hypo and hyper attenuation on axial CT. Right atrial or ventricular dilation Disparity of segmental vessels

Sensitivity and specificity of CTA imaging for CTEPH in one study from 2015 was 76% and 96 % respectively. A more recent meta-analysis from 2022 reported a much higher sensitivity of CTA of 98% with a similarly high specificity of 99%.

Direct hemodynamic measurement is required for the diagnosis for PAH.This is done via a right heart catheterization. The right atrial, right ventricular, mean pulmonary artery, and pulmonary capillary wedge pressures are directly measured, and pulmonary vascular resistance is calculated.
This step is essential for classifying the type of PH based on hemodynamic characteristics and to confirm the presence of PH prior to initiating treatment.
Hemodynamic assessment including vasoreactivity testing, helps to determine which patients are candidates for high dose calcium channel blocker therapy.
PAH (idiopathic, hereditary and drug induced) patients who responded to vasoreactivity testing should receive high dose calcium channel blockers.C

Several PAH specific medications are now available for the treatment of group 1 PAH, these medications are indicated for WHO functional class 3 or 4 and those who have not had adequate clinical response to high dose calcium channel blockers.C
Patients with CTEPH should be on life-long anticoagulation. The primary treatment options for CTEPH now include pulmonary endarterectomy.C
Most of the causes of PH can be managed by treating the underlying disease, for example group 2 PH is best treated by optimizing heart failure therapy. C

In adults with PH, the decision to refer for pulmonary rehabilitation is optional. There is more evidence for pulmonary rehabilitation in patient's with both stable COPD and after hospitalization for COPD exacerbation.C

Guidelines suggest patients with PAH should be physically active within symptom limits and should avoid excessive exertion. They should also be vaccinated against pneumococcal and influenza infections.
Patients in this group should have vasoreactivity testing and those who do not respond to acute vasoreactivity testing should be risk stratified based on their cardiopulmonary comorbidities.

Over the past 2 decades, several advancements have been made in the medical management of pulmonary artery hypertension. As of 2015 there were 14 Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved drugs that interact with the three main pathological mechanisms of PAH namely prostacyclin, nitric oxide, and endothelin pathways
See for a summary of drugs used to treat PAH.
Includes high doses of nifedipine (120-240 mg), amlodipine (20 mg) or diltiazem (240-720mg)

The 2022 guidelines from the European Respiratory Society (ERS) recommend using high dose calcium channel blockers in patients with PAH (idiopathic, hereditary or drug related) who respond well to acute vasoreactivity testing. They are contraindicated in patients who do not respond well to acute vasoreactivity testing.
A study of 557 patients with IPAH showed that only a small percentage (<10%) of patients have a long-term response to calcium channel blockers.
Older studies show a modest improvement in survival when calcium channel blockers were used in patients with pulmonary hypertension, however there is no new data to confirm these findings.
Limitations are hypotension, lower extremity edema and right ventricular failure
These drugs block the effect of endothelin thereby reducing pulmonary vasoconstriction. Ambrisentan acts on endothelin A , while bosentan and macitentan act on endothelin B.
Ambrisentan and bosentan showed improvement in exercise capacity as seen by an improvement in 6 minute walk distance (6MWD) which has been shown in placebo-controlled trials.

A randomized control trial of 742 patients reported reduced morbidity with macitentan as a composite outcome (worsening of pulmonary arterial hypertension, initiation of treatment with intravenous or subcutaneous prostanoids, lung transplantation, or atrial septostomy). This study did not show a statistically significant improvement in mortality and included a large portion of patients (60%) who were already receiving therapy for PAH. In a subsequent study 5-year survival with macitentan was estimated to be 83.3% with a similar safety profile.
Hepatic dysfunction is a common adverse effect of treatment. Macitetan has an increased risk of reduction in hemoglobin.
These drugs increase nitric oxide in the pulmonary vasculature resulting in pulmonary vasodilation. Examples include sildenafil, tadalafil and vardenafil

Previous studies of sildenafil and tadalafil showed a significant improvement in exercise capacity, WHO functional class and hemodynamics. Of note the improvement was not apparent in patients who were on background therapy with ERA’s and then treated with tadalafil.
Follow up studies showed that 60% of the patients treated with sildenafil maintained their functional class and 46% maintained or improved their exercise capacity (6-minute walk).

An RCT of 500 participants randomized them to to the endothelin receptor antagonist ambrisentan, tadalafil, or both. The primary endpoint of clinical failure occurred less often in the combined therapy groups than in the monotherapy groups (18% versus 28%-34%, NNT = 8). The 6MWD was also improved. A recent subgroup analysis of these patients with CTD PAH demonstrated a risk reduction of 51.7% with combination therapy when compared to sildenafil monotherapy.

An analysis of the GoDeep meta registry looked at 836 patients with a diagnosis of COPD with pulmonary hypertension. Of those patients, 418 received phosphodiestersase 5 inhibitors and showed a significant reduction in mortality with a hazard ratio of 0.65 (IQR, 0.57-0.75) for the entire cohort of patients with COPD and PH.
A small study that compared bosentan and sildenafil found that they were similarly effective in patients with moderately severe PAH.
Flushing, headaches, and epistaxis are common side effects
cGMP stimulators act by causing pulmonary vasodilation.

Riociguat is a soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator. In a study of 443 patients, there were improvements in the 36 meter walk, Borg dyspnea score, and the "Living with Pulmonary Hypertension" score. In a subgroup analysis of patients who weren't on background therapy Riociguat showed an improvement in exercise tolerance (improved six-minute walk 6MWD) and well as delayed clinical worsening.
Headache was reported as the most common adverse side effect.

Potent pulmonary vasodilator such as epoprostenol, iloprost and treprostinil. Treprostinil is available in subcutaneous, inhalational and oral formulations. The efficacy of this medication varies based on the route of administration.

Data on oral treprostinil is mixed with the best evidence for oral treprostinil when it is used in patients who were already taking monotherapy (an endothelin receptor antagonist or a phosphodiesterase inhibitor). In this population based on RCT data, clinical worsening occurred less often in the oral treprostinil group than in placebo participants (26% vs 36%, HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.56-0.97; NNT of 10).

In a 16 week RCT of 326 patients comparing the prostacyclin analog treprostinil with placebo, worsening occurred less often in the treatment group (22.7% vs 33.1%, p = 0.04, NNT = 10). Patients also did 31 meters better on the 6 minute walk test.

Epoprostenol has a very short half-life and needs to be administered as a continuous infusion. It was the first disease specific treatment that showed improvement in survival in a randomized control trial involving patients with severe PAH.
In a study that included 203 patients with PAH and NYHA class 3 or 4, treated with inhaled iloprost, the primary end-point was met by 16.8% vs 4.9% compared to placebo (p = 0.007).

A trial randomized 326 patients with pulmonary hypertension due to interstitial lung diisease to inhaled treprostinil or placebo. After 16 weeks there was a greater improvement by 31 meteres in the 6 minute walk test in the treatment group. Clinical worsening also occurred significantly less often in the treprostinil group (22% vs 33%, p = .04, NNT = 9).
Flushing, headache, diarrhea, and leg pains are common side effects
These drugs increase pulmonary vasodilation.

Selexipag is a prostacyclin agonist, and in a placebo controlled RCT with 1156 patients reduced the likelihood of a composite of death or complications (27.0% vs 41.6%, p < 0.001, NNT = 7). However, most of the benefit was due to fewer complications, mortality was unchanged, and more patients discontinued the study drug due to adverse events (NNH = 14).
Headache, diarrhea, nausea and jaw pain are common side effects

listitem.em: An approach to management of patients with Group 1 PH (PAH)

list.listitem: See the suggested treatment algorithm in
PAH patients should be referred to PH centers of excellence.

Newly diagnosed patients with PAH (IPAH/HPAH/DPAH) should undergo vasoreactivity testing during their right heart catheterization. Patients who respond to vasodilators should receive high dose calcium channel blockers.

Patients who do not respond to vasodilators or who fail CCB therapy (when reassessed at 1 year after initiating treatment) should be assessed for cardiopulmonary comorbidities that will help determine the next steps.

Patients should be stratified into low, intermediate or high-risk groups (three strata model). This stratification model includes both subjective (syncope, WHO functional class etc.) and objective data (6-minute walk distance, echocardiography and hemodynamic studies).
Initial combination therapy with an endothelin receptor antagonist (ERA) and a PDE 5 inhibitor is recommended for patients with low or intermediate risk who do not have cardiopulmonary comorbidities.

In a event-driven, double-blind study with 500 participants, the combination of ambrisentan and tadalafil was compared to monotherapy with either drug alone. Primary endpoint (first event of clinical failure) occurred in 18% of combination group and 31% of pooled monotherapy group (NNT = 8).

In addition to the above studies a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study that included 247 patients compared dual (macitentan/tadalafil) to triple therapy (macitentan/tadalafil/selexepag) did not show any significant benefit of triple therapy over dual therapy.
There are no evidence-based recommendations for patients with cardiopulmonary comorbidities, however current guidelines suggest that PDEi5 or an ERA should be considered in these patients.

At subsequent follow ups patients should be further stratified based on the 4 strata model to help determine subsequent management. More information regarding this can be found at the 2022 ECC/ERS Guidelines.
Group 2 PH treatment primarily involves optimizing heart function, aggressive guideline directed heart failure therapy and repair of valvular heart disease if indicated.

Inhaled treprostinil has been studied in 326 patients with PH secondary to interstitial lung disease. When compared with placebo clinical worsening occurred significantly less often in the treprostinil group compared to placebo (22.7% vs 33.1%, NNT = 10). Current guidelines suggest use of inhaled treprostinil in this subset of patients with interstitial lung disease related pulmonary hypertension.
Otherwise no specific treatment options are available for patients with PH secondary to lung disease. Long term oxygen supplementation has been shown to decrease the progression of disease in COPD.
Based on expert consensus patients with CTEPH should be on lifelong anticoagulation with Vitamin K antagonists.

In a randomized control trial of riociguat that included 261 CTEPH patients who were not surgical candidates or who had recurrent PH after pulmonary endarterectomy, Riociguat improved 6MWD by 39 meters as compared to a decreased 6MWD of 6 meters in the placebo group.

In a randomized control trial of subcutaneous treprostinil that included 105 patients with CTEPH that were not surgical candidates. High dose treprostinil improved the 6MWD by 45 meters (95% CI 27 to 62 meters).
Riociguat and subcutaeous treprostenil can be used as medical management in CTEPH patients who are not surgical candidates or who had persistence or recurrence of PH after surgery.

In a multicenter double blinded phase 3 trial comparing patients with PH WHO class ll or lll who were receiving stable background therapy, the addition of sotatercept compared to placebo resulted in a greater improvement in exercise capacity in the sotatercept group (as assessed by the 6-minute walk test) than placebo.The Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the difference between the sotatercept and placebo groups in the change from baseline at week 24 in the 6-minute walk distance was 40.8 m (95% CI, 27.5 to 54.1; P<0.001).
Depending on the PH group, different surgical options may be available.

Early referral to lung transplant center should be considered in Group 1 PH patients who are identified to be deteriorating during structured follow-up assessments. Patients who fail initial combination therapy, patients on triple therapy and high-risk patients (1 year mortality >10%) are all candidates for lung transplant.
Patients with Group 2 PH may need surgical procedures to correct defective valves and may benefit from left ventricular assist devices

In patients with Group 4 PH, surgery is the primary treatment option. Pulmonary artery endarterectomy is potentially curative. Patients experience significant improvement in symptoms, right heart function and hemodynamic parameters after the surgery. Balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) is a potential alternative in patients who are poor surgical candidates.
Evidence regarding the efficacy of balloon atrial septoplasty for patients with advanced PH is limited, with improvements in before/after studies only seen in the short-term.

In patients with Group 1 PH balloon atrial septostomy (BAS) is considered a palliative or bridging procedure. BAS use in advanced PAH can have beneficial hemodynamic effects like reductions in right atrial pressures.
Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and right ventricular assist devices can also be used as a bridge to lung transplantation

In patients with inoperable Group 4 pulmonary hypertension who were symptomatic with a residual PVR > 4 WU, a post hoc analysis from the RACE trial showed that both riociguat and balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) significantly improved cardiac output, stroke volume, and RV afterload. The relative changes in RV afterload from baseline to week 26 were more pronounced in the BPA group (all P<0.001).

Hospitalization and admission may be required in WHO functional class IV PAH patients with hypotension (systolic blood pressure < 90), tachycardia (heart rate > 110), decreased urine output, and elevated lactate levels.

Early referral to a PH center of excellence should be considered in patients with severe PH and right heart failure. Patients needing surgical interventions also need to be referred to expert centers.

When initial treatment approach results in worsening of patient's clinical condition (with regards to symptoms of right heart failure, syncopal events, exercise tolerance, WHO functional class, biochemical and imaging findings) patients should be considered for transplant center referral.
Patients on maximal triple therapy should also be considered for lung transplantation.
The diagnosis of PH irrespective of the class of PH increases the risk of mortality by 7-fold.C
Compared to patients with idiopathic PAH, patients with PAH associated with connective tissue diseases and HIV disease have a worse prognosis. C
Outcomes and progression of disease varies among different diagnostic groups.
PH can serve as a strong predictor of mortality in patients with pulmonary fibrosis.
Mortality among patients with PH is 62.4 % at 5 years 9. PH is more severe in patients older than 60 years.
The European society defines high risk PAH patients as those with mortality >10%. The REVEAL 2 .0 score can be reliably used to risk stratify patient with PAH.
1 year mortality for group 2 PH and group 3 PH is 41% and 46% respectively.
Mild PH is also associated with an increased risk of mortality.

According to the COMPERA registry, the risk of mortality in patients with PAH increases as the severity of the disease worsens. Tthe observed mortality rate 1 year after diagnosis of low-risk PAH being 2.8%, 9.9% in the intermediate-risk, and 21.2% in the high-risk category.

Among venous thromboembolic disease patients, a Danish study reported a higher mortality rate in patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) as compared to those without CTEPH, 121 per 1,000 person-years.
In a systematic review, patients with systemic sclerosis associated PH had higher mortality compared to patients with systemic sclerosis without PH.
The goal for therapy is to achieve a low-risk state, guidelines recommend assessing patients' risk at each follow up visit.

Various clinical data (symptoms of right heart failure, WHO functional status, 6 Minute walk distance), laboratory data (Brain natriuretic peptide levels), imaging findings (right atrial area, pericardial effusion) and hemodynamic measurements (Right atrial pressure, cardiac index and SvO2) must be obtained during follow up visits.
Patients who are treated with CCB’s should have complete reassessment including a right heart catheterization in 3-4 months after initiation of therapy.
Patients with PAH should avoid pregnancy.
Patients who continue with pregnancy with PAH should be managed in centers with experience in managing their unique clinical course.

Children with PAH with right heart failure or hypercoagulable state should get anticoagulation with warfarin. Children with PAH without right heart failure or with hypercoagulable state should get anticoagulation with warfarin. For children <5 years old, lower target international normalized ratios (INR) are recommended.

When suspected, initial evaluation includes history, physical examination, ECG, echocardiogram, pulmonary function tests, and chest x-ray. If no obvious underlying cardiovascular or pulmonary cause for PAH is detected, then cardiac catheterization or cardiac MRI should be considered.
Guidelines for the management of pediatric PAH have been published by the American Heart Association and American Thoracic Society, and are available online here.

algorithm.title: Initial Management Algorithm for Pulmonary Artery Hypertension

cell.label: Oral anticoagulant, especially if idiopathic PAH (IPAH), diuretics oxygen. Perform acute vasoreactivity testing during catheterization.
Oral CCB, especially if IPAH. Sustained response?
Sildenafil, treprostinil SC, or treprostinil IV.
Bosentan, sildenafil, eporostenol, iloprost, treprostinil SC, or treprostinil IV.
Epoprostenol IV, bosentan, Iloprost, sildenafil, treprostinil SC, or treprostinil IV.
Patient fails to improve or deteriorates.
Consider: 1. Combination of bosentan, sildenafil, and prostanoid. 2. Referral for atrioseptostomy or lung transplant.

tr.td: Combined pre and post capillary PH
Right ventricle to Left ventricle ratio > 1.0 Interventricular septal flattening
RV outflow doppler acceleration time < 105 msec Mid diastolic notching Early diastolic pulmonary regurgitation velocity >2.2 m/sec Pulmonary artery diameter > 25mm
C: Inferior vena cava (IVC) and right atrium
IVC diameter > 21 mm with decreased inspiratory collapse (<50% with sniff or <20% with quiet inspiration)Right atrial area at end systole >18 cm
Prostacyclin Analogues: epoprostenol, iloprost, treprostinil, beraprost
Endothelin Receptor Antagonists: ambrisentan, bosentan, macitentan
